Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

exclude verb

also exclusion, leave out, shut out, rule out, keep out, excluding

classical

Cic. Off. 1.134: nec vērō … exclūdat aliōs
Quint. 1.1.26: nōn exclūdō, I don’t rule it out

exclūdō, exclūdere, exclūsī, exclūsum

verb, third conjugation, transitive; ab + abl., or the abl. alone

shut out, keep out, exclude; rule out

To shut someone out of a place, a talk or a share: Gādītānī Poenōs moenibus exclūsērunt (Cic. Balb. 39; Lewis & Short). It is also the word for a hen hatching chicks (Comenius, after Cicero).

Other words

  • praetermittō, praetermittere, praetermīsī, praetermissum — leave out, omit, pass over

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.111: quod verba sint praetermissa (Lewis & Short)

    Leaving out in speaking or writing, or letting a chance go by.

  • excipiō, excipere, excēpī, exceptum — except, make an exception of

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical

    Excluding from a rule or a list: see exception.

Examples

  • nec vērō, tamquam in possessiōnem suam vēnerit, exclūdat aliōs, sed cum reliquīs in rēbus, tum in sermōne commūnī vicissitūdinem nōn inīquam putet

    and he should not shut others out, as if he had come into his own property, but think it fair, in conversation as in everything else, to take turnsCic. Off. 1.134

  • nōn exclūdō autem, id quod est inventum irrītandae ad discendum īnfantiae grātiā, eburneās etiam litterārum fōrmās in lūsum offerre

    I don’t rule out the thing invented to tempt small children to learn, giving them ivory letters to play withQuint. 1.1.26

See also exception, except, isolate.
